FP8 reduces storage/bandwidth and can accelerate matrix multiplication on supported hardware, while sensitive reductions, master parameters, and accumulations often remain at higher precision. E4M3 allocates more mantissa precision with less range; E5M2 offers a wider exponent range with coarser precision. Forward/backward format choices depend on the framework and architecture rather than a universal fixed rule. Scaling maps tensor values into the representable range, and block/tile scaling accommodates local magnitude variation better than one global scale when outliers dominate. Too-small values underflow and too-large values overflow or saturate; scale tracking itself must be stable. Validate loss convergence, outlier channels, gradient statistics, and target quality. FP8 speedups depend on kernel support, communication, and whether the workload is compute-bound, not merely on halving element bytes.
